script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for MEME. Tuesday — here is your MEME recap. The portfolio closed up eight point six eight percent on the session. A strong day across nearly every position, driven by a catalyst that reshaped the optical networking landscape overnight.

A draft proposal out of Washington to ban Chinese-made optical components from American data centers hit the wires early Tuesday morning, and domestic suppliers moved immediately. Applied Optoelectronics surged nearly twenty percent before the session was done. The ban is not yet final — and that uncertainty matters.

No broad macro data was available for Tuesday's session. Markets appeared to trade on sector-specific and geopolitical news rather than any single index-level catalyst, though the technology-heavy Nasdaq composite was broadly constructive on the session, benefiting from the same tailwinds that lifted optical networking names and AI infrastructure plays throughout the day.

The lead story Tuesday belongs to the reported United States ban on Chinese data center optical hardware. According to reporting cited by multiple financial outlets, a draft proposal would restrict Chinese-made optical components used in domestic data centers, with an enforcement target before year-end. The report immediately lifted domestic optical suppliers. Applied Optoelectronics rocketed nineteen point four four percent. Lumentum gained eight point nine two percent. Coherent and Corning also moved sharply. The key caveat, flagged clearly in the reporting, is that this remains a draft — it can be softened or dropped entirely before enforcement. For holders of both Applied Optoelectronics and Lumentum in this portfolio, the position sizing means the combined move added meaningful upside Tuesday. The story to watch is whether the proposal advances toward formal rulemaking or quietly stalls.

Applied Optoelectronics was up nineteen point four four percent on the session. This was the single largest mover in the portfolio Tuesday, and the driver is clear — the reported Chinese optics ban sent domestic suppliers surging. Separately, the company announced it will present at Rosenblatt's Sixth Annual Technology Summit on August eighteenth via fireside chat, with the chief financial officer presenting. Zacks analysis also flagged that Applied Optoelectronics heads into second-quarter earnings with strong artificial intelligence-driven eight-hundred-G demand and cable television growth, though production constraints and valuation remain watch items. Earnings will be the next major catalyst.

Turning to Redwire Corporation, up ten point two seven percent on the session. The company heads into second-quarter earnings with projected sales growth of seventy point six percent and a record backlog, according to analyst commentary published Tuesday. Research and development spending may pressure near-term margins. Watch the earnings release closely for revenue recognition detail against that backlog figure.

Over at AST SpaceMobile, the stock was up ten point six nine percent on the session. Space stocks broadly surged Tuesday as traders positioned ahead of SpaceX's first-ever public earnings report. Prediction markets cited in financial press flagged a seventy percent probability of a miss on that report, and a lockup expiry involving hundreds of millions of shares looms within days — a setup that could cut either way for sector sentiment. AST SpaceMobile also faces its own second-quarter earnings release as a forward catalyst, with satellite launches and Federal Communications Commission approvals already in hand but execution risk still a concern for analysts.

Nebius Group was up six point one nine percent on the session. Piper Sandler named CoreWeave its top artificial intelligence cloud pick over Nebius, citing execution risk as the differentiator separating neocloud leaders. That is a headwind to watch at the analyst level, though Nebius still moved higher Tuesday alongside broader AI infrastructure enthusiasm.

Bloom Energy was up four point four eight percent on the session. No company-specific news drove the move — this appears to be a continuation of strength in the clean energy and data center power infrastructure theme that has supported the name. Watch for any commentary tied to data center power demand narratives as that story evolves.

TeraWulf was up zero point two seven percent on the session — the quietest mover in the portfolio Tuesday. The bitcoin mining and high-performance computing name largely sat out the day's rally. No company-specific news was available. Relative underperformance against the portfolio warrants monitoring.

Meanwhile, Lumentum Holdings was up eight point nine two percent on the session. The same Chinese optics ban report that lifted Applied Optoelectronics drove Lumentum sharply higher. Both names are domestic optical networking suppliers, and both benefited from the same draft policy headline. Watch for any formal regulatory update out of Washington.

IREN Limited was up two point seven seven percent on the session. The artificial intelligence data center and bitcoin mining infrastructure name moved modestly higher. No company-specific news was available Tuesday. Sector trends in high-performance computing infrastructure remain the primary driver to monitor.

Sandisk Corporation closed up ten point eight four percent on the session. A strong move for the flash storage name, though no specific company news was tied directly to the move. Watch for any supply chain or enterprise storage demand commentary that could provide fundamental context to Tuesday's gain.

Three items to watch in the next forty-eight hours. First, Applied Optoelectronics at Rosenblatt's Technology Summit on August eighteenth — management commentary could set near-term tone. Second, SpaceX's inaugural public earnings report, which moves the entire space sector and directly affects AST SpaceMobile. Third, any formal rulemaking update on the Chinese optical component ban, which is the single largest driver of portfolio performance Tuesday.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for MEME. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. Watch closely for any regulatory confirmation or denial on the Chinese optics ban — that one headline has the power to reverse Tuesday's largest gains just as fast as it created them.
